instruction: Please sort the transaction records by amount in descending order (highest to lowest).

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting Amount column (column D) in descending order. Verified with Python: 18 records, sorted descending from 9444 to 442. Evaluator extracts column D values and compares against expected descending sorted list.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Getter logic fundamentally flawed - it sorts the extracted values itself (line 46: sorted(values, reverse=True))
Verification bypass: The getter always returns sorted data regardless of whether the user actually sorted the spreadsheet
Cannot verify task completion: The evaluator will pass even if the user never performed any sorting operation
Wrong extraction approach: Getter should extract values in their ACTUAL order from the spreadsheet, not sort them programmatically
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Remove the sorting logic from getter (line 46): return 'values' directly instead of 'sorted_values'
Getter should extract column D values in their actual order as they appear in the spreadsheet
Metric should then compare the actual order against the expected sorted order to verify the user completed the sort task
The partial credit logic in metric (line 20-23) would then become meaningful - checking if data is sorted even if values differ
